candidates.title: Chaining Skills to Hijack LLM Agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CR cross-listed cs.AI), not peer reviewed
candidates.institution: The University of Hong Kong (lead), Shandong University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Southeast University
communitySignals: No public GitHub repo found; reproducibility statement references internal supplementary scripts only
credibilityEvidence: Table 2: ASR 54.8-90.3% across 24 model-family combinations, 512/690 (74.2%) aggregate
Section 4.3 Proposition 1: formal bound on false-allow/false-deny tradeoff for permission decisions from local record view
Section 4.4 Proposition 2: finite-state cost model for Work Loop token amplification (2.20x-36.39x)
Section 6.1 Table 3: structural ablation vs direct injection (3.5%) and monolithic workflow (17.4%) on GPT-5.4
Section 6.3 Table 4: taint-guided defense evaluation on both attack success and 72 benign-task utility
Appendix A: explicit Limitations section
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Covers 6 models, 4 attack families + 1 availability attack, formal theoretical bound, ablations on skill count and structural controls, and a defense evaluation with both attack and benign-utility metrics; still a controlled SkillsBench simulation rather than an observed in-the-wild incident.
reproducibilityEvidence: Reproducibility statement references 'supplementary data' and 'accompanying scripts' that regenerate result tables, but no public repository URL was found on the abstract page or in the paper text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Supports the narrow claim that, under this threat model and SkillsBench environment, attacker-controlled skill chains can induce unwanted actions at high rates while native task-verifier scores stay nearly unchanged, which is exactly the blind spot the article describes.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Results are reported per experimental condition rather than the joint per-run distribution of attack success and task utility, so a condition's near-baseline utility score does not guarantee every individual successful attack preserved useful work (Appendix A).
candidates.presentationReason: Threat model, attack families, metrics, and limitations are all explicitly delineated; formal propositions are stated and proved in the appendix.
candidates.reason: Selected as the security angle: directly exposes a supply-chain blind spot in the fast-growing Agent Skill ecosystem (Claude Skills, GPT-6 Astra skills, SkillsMP-style marketplaces), with a concrete, formally characterized mechanism (task-progress record carrying a false approval claim across skills) and across-model empirical validation that native verifier scores fail to catch.

candidates.title: Agents Are Systems, Not Models: Rethinking Agentic Evaluation
candidates.institution: Technical University of Munich / MCML / Helmholtz Munich (lead), Inria / ENS / CNRS / PSL Research University
communitySignals: GitHub repo (lusxvr/rethinking-agent-evaluation) exists but currently holds only README/.gitignore; authors state code and 18,240 trajectories will be released
credibilityEvidence: Section 4.1: full factorial design, 432 configurations x 5 repeats x 4 tasks = 8,640 main-experiment runs
Table 2/3: per-task completion rate, hurdle-clearing rate, and axis-effect ranking with bootstrap robustness check (Information ranks first in >=99% of bootstrap samples)
Section 4.3: ablations across two further model families (Step-3.7-Flash, Claude Sonnet 5) and an oracle-verification-tool ablation
Section 5: independently validated behavior taxonomy via embedding+clustering pipeline cross-tabulated against experimental conditions
Explicit Limitations paragraph in Section 6
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Large factorial design with repeated runs specifically built to measure variance (not just point estimates), plus cross-model-family and open-vs-closed-model ablations; explicitly limited to 4 tasks across 2 scientific domains and excludes memory/multi-agent coordination as configuration axes.
reproducibilityEvidence: Authors commit to releasing code, the benchmark, and 18,240 agent trajectories with produced artifacts; GitHub repo exists but was not yet populated with code at time of reading
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The core quantitative claim (~54% of outcome variance among genuine attempts is run-to-run noise, not configuration) is directly measured from the repeated-run design itself, independent of any external baseline comparison, which is the strongest form of support available for that specific claim.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Covers only 4 tasks across 2 scientific domains (astrophysics, genomics); the finding that some behaviors (verification) respond more to system design than prompting is demonstrated on one behavioral dimension and the authors caution it is not yet a general principle.
candidates.presentationReason: Axes, metrics, and benchmark construction are precisely defined with formal notation; limitations are stated directly by the authors rather than implied.
candidates.reason: Selected as the evaluation/limits angle: the ~54% run-to-run-noise finding is a directly actionable warning for anyone reading a single-run agent benchmark number (including the daily digest's own past coverage of single-run leaderboard deltas), and the axis-interaction findings (information > budget > model size) give a concrete, testable priority order for agent builders.

candidates.title: Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CL cross-listed cs.AI), not peer reviewed
candidates.institution: The University of Texas at Austin, AIDAChip Inc.
communitySignals: GitHub repo (AIDAChip-Inc/mem-plus-plus) is live with a substantive README describing architecture, usage and results
credibilityEvidence: Section 3: formal architecture (store + consolidation operator + read operator with weighted RRF fusion and recency reserve)
Table 1/2/3: evaluated against 7 baselines (Full Context, RAG-4096, Mem0, Zep, A-Mem, LangMem, gbrain) on 3 benchmarks (OrgMemBench, LoCoMo, LongMemEval_S) with 2 answering models
Section 4.3 Table 4: ablation on retrieval legs, write-time processing, and entity-graph variant showing write-time LLM calls add no consistent gain
Explicit 'Where Mem++ Trails' subsection naming the categories where RAG and Nemori outperform it
Conclusion explicitly flags the organizational result rests on only 73 questions from one synthetic benchmark
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Method and ablations are clear and the comparison set is reasonably broad, but the primary organizational-memory claim rests on only 73 questions over one synthetic organization (OrgMemBench medium tier), and the method is outright beaten by RAG on 2 of 6 categories (Contradiction, Bi-temporal) and by Nemori on several conversational sub-metrics.
reproducibilityEvidence: Benchmark evaluation code is publicly released at github.com/AIDAChip-Inc/mem-plus-plus; full system promised 'upon publication' is not yet separately confirmed live
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Supports the narrow, hedged claim that keeping documents whole and deferring version selection to read time beats write-time LLM-distillation on the tested organizational and conversational benchmarks, but the modest overall margins (2.6-13.1 points) and the small synthetic organizational benchmark mean the 'best architecture' framing needs explicit hedging in the article.
candidates.primaryLimitation: The organizational-memory evaluation (the paper's main contribution) rests on only 73 questions against one synthetic organization; the authors themselves note this and plan to collect more diverse real organizational records.
candidates.presentationReason: Method notation, baselines, and where the method loses are all stated directly, including an explicit section naming the categories where it underperforms.
candidates.reason: Selected as the method/capability angle to complete the day's three-angle coverage (security, evaluation, memory): the core design principle (do not spend an LLM call compressing memory at write time; store documents whole and let retrieval plus a recency reserve decide at read time) is directly actionable for teams building long-term/organizational agent memory, even though the evidence is narrower and more hedged than the other two selections.
